default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-178.title: Liquidity-clock break fade
E-178.hypothesis: When the seasonal bar range for this minute (20-session median) is clearly below its level 30 minutes earlier, the session is entering a quieter part of its daily liquidity clock (participants leaving); a close beyond the recent high/low then has no arriving flow behind it and is faded by liquidity providers.

E-179.title: Separation-bar follow in a sticky tape
E-179.hypothesis: When consecutive bars have overlapped heavily for a while, makers quote a two-sided book; a bar trading entirely beyond the previous bar (no overlap at all) means an initiator cleared every resting quote at once, and makers widen and step away in that direction, so follow the separation.

E-180.title: Morning-value afternoon reversion
E-180.hypothesis: The VWAP of the morning (before 12:00) is the price where the cash-session participants built the day's inventory; an afternoon stretch far from it is carried by the thinner afternoon crowd, and the first counter bar starts the return toward the morning value as morning holders defend and afternoon chasers exit.

E-181.title: Elder impulse colour flip follow
E-181.hypothesis: Elder's Impulse System colours a bar green when both the 13-EMA and the MACD histogram rise and red when both fall, and its many users act on the colour; the first green bar after a red one means both inertia and momentum turned together, the red-bar sellers are stopped and impulse users buy at once, so follow it.

E-182.title: VWAP-agreement balance micro-break fade
E-182.hypothesis: When the volume-weighted price of the last window sits on top of the session VWAP, recent trade is happening at the day's average cost: the market is in balance around value and no one is migrating it; a close beyond the last 15 minutes' high/low in that state is a small push that responsive traders fade.

E-183.title: Yesterday-range step expansion follow
E-183.hypothesis: Day traders gauge today's progress in units of yesterday's range; each time today's range crosses a further fixed fraction of it on a new session extreme, the stops of those who sized for a day like yesterday sit just beyond and expansion traders add, so follow the bar that makes the new step.

E-184.title: Elder force-index dip in an EMA trend
E-184.hypothesis: Elder's force index (price change x volume, short EMA) going negative inside a rising trend shows a pullback with sellers committing volume; when it turns back positive while price still holds above the trend EMA, the volume-backed selling is done and trend holders resume, so buy (mirror in a down trend).

E-185.title: Woodies CCI zero-line reject
E-185.hypothesis: In Woodies CCI, a CCI that was recently above +100 and pulls back toward but not through the zero line, then hooks up, marks a shallow correction inside an intact push; the CCI traders buy the hook together and the faders' stops sit just above, so follow the hook (mirror below zero).

E-186.title: Close-pin release follow
E-186.hypothesis: Several bars in a row closing at almost the same price while still trading a range mean a large limit order is pinning that price and absorbing both sides; a bar that then closes a full typical range away shows the pin was filled or pulled, and the side it was holding back runs, so follow the release bar.

E-187.title: Ehlers Fisher transform extreme turn fade
E-187.hypothesis: The Fisher transform of the price's position in its recent range turns the bounded position into a near-Gaussian score that makes extremes sharp; when it turns down from a high extreme, the short-term buyers who pushed price to the top of its window stopped paying up and the many Fisher users sell the turn, so fade (mirror from a low extreme).
